Fortress uniform/equipment selector — native PE source grammar

Source: data/runtime/native-pe-images.json reference and classic files. This
inventory reads the binaries on disk; it does not attach to a game process.
pe-functions.tsv records each source path, PE identity, SHA-256, complete owner
extent, executable extent, and assembly filename. pe-unwind-fragments.tsv
retains the original CHAININFO splits. pe-*-ghidra-decompiled.c and the per-role
.c files contain actual Ghidra C generated from these native instruction bodies.

Native entry points (RVAs)
reference renderer: 450140..459394 (executable end 4590fc)
classic renderer:   44dd00..456f54 (executable end 456cbc)
reference population: 45f570..463495 (executable end 4633ec)
classic population:   45d130..461055 (executable end 460fac)
reference pointer input: 4593a0..45ddfd
classic pointer input:   456f60..45b9bd
The original table bytes remain part of each unwind extent and are represented
as selector aliases in pe-switches.tsv; they are not decoded as instructions.

Selector modes
0 bodywear type (item_type 19 hex)
1 headwear type (1c)
2 legwear type (3c)
3 handwear type (1d)
4 footwear type (1a)
5 shield type (1b)
6 weapon type (18)
7 material for selected equipment entry
8 color and dye
9 specific bodywear item
10 specific headwear item
11 specific legwear item
12 specific handwear item
13 specific footwear item
14 specific shield item
15 specific weapon item
pe-modes.tsv associates every mode with both editions' original dispatch and
case target. Values above 15 follow the native cleanup/default path.

Native panel state
The renderer first requires panel+145 != 0. A panel+294 category other than -1
selects the type list; otherwise panel+300 selects material, panel+350 color,
and panel+390 specific items. The remaining branch is the uniform editor.
The list initializer clears all four sets of vectors and resets row scroll and
hover state before the mode switch. No spelling-based category inference occurs.

Type list text and construction
A row whose item_type is -1 renders one of:
specific armor | specific helm | specific pants | specific gloves |
specific shoes | specific shield | specific weapon
This sentinel row is populated when panel+148 != -1.
Otherwise flags bit 0 renders individual choice, adding ', weapon' for type 18;
bit 1 renders indiv choice, melee; bit 2 renders indiv choice, ranged.
All other rows call the complete generic item-type caption supplier using the
actual item_type/subtype. A separate native bit vector appends ' (foreign)'.
The population takes civilization-specific subtype vectors first, then appends
raw item definitions not already present and marks those appended rows foreign.
The weapon mode reads both native weapon subtype vectors. The complete native
loops, duplicate decisions, vector guards and every flag write are retained in
uniform-equipment-all-selector-choice-population.c/.asm for each edition.
The generic supplier is a82c10..a882fc reference / a7fc90..a8537c classic;
its complete switch includes all game item types, while this selector supplies
the seven equipment types listed above.

Material list text and filtering
A concrete material type/index calls 14d1920 reference / 14cc890 classic.
Otherwise category -1 produces any material. The category switch includes
leather, cloth, silk, yarn, plant fiber, metal, wood, stone, gem, bone, shell,
pearl, tooth, horn; unmapped values use BROKEN.
Mode 7 reads the selected equipment type/subtype from panel+1b8/+1d0.
A selected type -1 returns without filling a material list.
For body/head/leg/hand/foot types, an unspecified subtype allows material
categories 10,1,1b,1c,1d (hex). A defined subtype reads its raw definition flags:
bit index 0 adds 1b/1c/1d, index 2 adds 10, index 5 adds 1.
Shield adds categories 3/10. The original remap table also records all default
aliases for the item_type switch (type minus 19 hex).
The list always begins with (-1,-1,-1), the any-material tuple. Category rows
follow, then concrete native material vectors. The category-to-vector remap
covers leather, metal, wood, plant fiber, silk and yarn; metal enumeration
requires both native material flags 2f and 38. Weapon material handling has
additional raw subtype fields e8, d2, 108/110 and material fields 284, 290/298:
material flag byte 5 must exist and be negative; flag byte 6 bits 08 or 10 are
alternate candidates; material field 284 > 9999 is the other candidate. A
defined weapon subtype further gates these branches with subtype d2 != -1 or
with a nonempty subtype field 108/110 and its first flag bit. An e8 weapon
field enables wood/bone category rows and the accompanying native organic
material vectors. An unspecified weapon subtype permits the general versions
of these candidates. These compound AND/OR expressions are retained literally
in Ghidra mode case 7, including all NULL/length conditions and default edges.
pe-conditions.tsv and pe-branches.tsv preserve each original comparison/test
and taken/fallthrough address without replacing these native bit meanings with
guessed item/material flag names.

Color list text and filtering
Mode 8 begins with color id -1 (any color), dye flag false. It converts the
native dye-material vectors to color ids, skips -1 and duplicates, and marks
those rows as dyes. It then adds remaining descriptor patterns whose short
field +38 equals 0, skipping any already inserted color id. The renderer
resolves the pattern's first color id and calls a frameless color-name leaf:
reference 420fc0..42101f / classic 41eb80..41ebdf. It copies descriptor+50.
Dye rows append ' (Dye)'. The leaf's range is decoded directly; it has no
exception-unwind record of its own.

Specific-item list filtering and sort (modes 9..15)
Each mode iterates its type-specific native item-id vector and the native
second item-id vector. Stale ids are removed by the original native code.
A candidate is retained only if all conditions below hold:
- item pointer resolves;
- (DWORD item+10 & 20) == 0;
- (BYTE item+14 & 08) == 0;
- (DWORD item+10 & e90c10) == 0;
- item id is absent from the native global exclusion vector at 142399860
  reference (the classic address is retained in that edition's native body);
- the complete delegated eligibility predicate c93160 returns false;
- item id is absent from panel+1a0, the current selection vector.
The delegated predicate is also fully decompiled, with its CHAININFO fragments:
c93160..c93373 reference. It rejects item flag 20000 or its delegated location
predicate. For the remaining item, it obtains effective coordinates from direct
position or native contained/unit/building references; invalid coordinates,
missing map/block data and flag-10 cases return false, while a resolved map
block returns bit 9 of the tile value at block+2a0. The location predicate at
c93060..c93152 traverses container references or delegates a unit predicate and
can read a type-7 reference's byte +a. Both predicates and their exact native
conditions/callees are preserved as source rather than assigned guessed names.
For each retained candidate, virtual method +6d8 supplies its sort key, stored
at item+5c. The native comparator sorts larger keys first, with pointer/null
special cases, then the list stores the sorted item ids in panel+398.

Specific-item text supplier
Missing pointers render missing item. Existing items call the complete native
caption supplier c65450..c65f0a reference / c62490..c62f4a classic.
The original owner is split after c6571d reference / c6275d classic by native
CHAININFO; those fragments are joined for actual C decompilation, including
the post-split virtual +5f0 description and all quality, wear, ownership and
special glyph branches. Named artifacts and native copy/name branches precede
the ordinary virtual description. Literal ' (copy)' and every fixed operand
are indexed in pe-literals.tsv. Native glyph character writes remain visible
in both complete assembly and actual Ghidra C.

Assignment text and custom squad names
The item-assignment row can be:
Will be assigned to {squad}, position {one-based position}
Assigned to {squad}, position {one-based position}
Assigned
A nonempty squad+80 is copied directly. Only an empty alias calls the existing
native generated-name supplier on squad+8. A custom squad alias is data and
must be preserved exactly; it is never an untranslated interface branch.

Display writers and native clipping
pe-display-fields.tsv records both editions' five addst call/return sites:
EquipmentType, Material, Color, Item, Assignment. The first four fields use
native width clipping before addst and may end in three literal dots. This is
part of the original text production, rather than an independent text branch.

Source index
pe-functions.tsv: complete source body extent, identity and digest
pe-unwind-fragments.tsv: original unwind fragments and parent ownership
pe-modes.tsv: all 0..15 original selector cases
pe-switches.tsv: complete native selector aliases and jump destinations
pe-conditions.tsv: every original cmp/test/bt operand
pe-branches.tsv: conditional/unconditional taken and fallthrough addresses
pe-calls.tsv: direct native calls/tail calls
pe-literals.tsv: literal operands, including the uniform editor adjacent states
pe-display-fields.tsv: native writer sites and dynamic field origins
pe-{edition}-{role}.asm/.c: complete original bodies and actual Ghidra C
pe-{edition}-ghidra-decompiled.c: complete edition C source aggregate
